heading: Who has John 18:31?
scope: Greek papyri and majuscules to AD 900
translation_note: Greek as printed in modern critical editions; the translation is our own, kept literal. Individual manuscripts differ in spelling, abbreviations and small wording details, and several preserve only a few letters of the verse.

verses.translation: So Pilate said to them, “Take him yourselves and judge him by your own law.” The Jews said to him, “It is not lawful for us to put anyone to death.”
verses.greek: Εἶπεν οὖν αὐτοῖς ὁ Πιλᾶτος· λάβετε αὐτὸν ὑμεῖς καὶ κατὰ τὸν νόμον ὑμῶν κρίνατε αὐτόν. εἶπον αὐτῷ οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι· ἡμῖν οὐκ ἔξεστιν ἀποκτεῖναι οὐδένα·

excluded.label: 05 D (Codex Bezae)
excluded.reason: The original Greek leaves for John 18:14–20:13 are lost. The gap was filled in later by another hand, so the text here is not the 5th-century copy.

excluded.label: 022 N (Petropolitanus Purpureus)
excluded.reason: The purple codex is scattered across several libraries; nothing survives between John 16:15 and 20:23.

excluded.label: 024 P (Guelferbytanus A)
excluded.reason: A palimpsest; only John 1:29–40, 2:13–25 and 21:1–11 survive.

excluded.label: 029 T (Borgianus)
excluded.reason: Greek text of John survives only as far as 8:31.

excluded.label: 031 V (Mosquensis II)
excluded.reason: The majuscule hand stops at John 8:39; the rest was supplied in minuscule in the 13th century.

excluded.label: 𝔓90
excluded.reason: Starts at John 18:36, just after our verse.

excluded.label: 028 S, 033 X, 036 Γ, 0141
excluded.reason: All contain John 18 but fall after the AD 900 cut-off for this first version. (028 S is precisely dated to 949 by its scribe’s note.)

excluded.label: Minuscules & lectionaries
excluded.reason: Hundreds of later copies contain the verse. They are planned for a later version as a searchable list.
